newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen steady, new listings leading.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen steady, new listings leading.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen steady on Thursday with interest staying in newly listed and electronics stocks, dealers said.
"The new listings are about the only game in town these days," said a dealer with a local firm.
Activity was expected to be bouyant with shares in Poh Lian Holdings due to begin trading today after its initial public offer was 33 times subscribed.
Thin trade on Wednesday saw the Straits Times Industrials Index hover around the 2,100 resistance level and it ended down 14.71 points at 2,098.26.
Interest in Singapore Airlines (SIA) could also be raised after a report in the Australian Financial Review said SIA could take equity in Australia's Ansett in order to fulfil its regional ambitions.
SIA has previously confirmed it is in talks with Ansett and Air New Zealand to establish a "commercial relationship" but said in April it was "premature to speculate on the outcome".
SIA shares stood at S$7.55 at Wednesday's close.
